headline: US stocks closed lower as AI trade unwound and Brent crude neared $110, driving rotation into energy following industrial production data
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 ($SPX) fell just over 1%, the Nasdaq ($COMP) dropped about 2.2% for its worst weekly performance since June, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DJI) slipped roughly 0.3%, and the Russell 2000 (IWM) lost about 1.7%.
- CoreWeave (CRWV) sank about 12% on renewed debt and leverage concerns after Morningstar cut its price target, with co-founders having sold $3.3 billion of stock since the IPO and its bonds trading in distressed territory with yields around 15%.
- Palantir (PLTR)’s recent breakout reversed, with shares down about 7% after a Bloomberg report on Democratic subpoena risk, while software names including Twilio (TWLO), which dropped about 11%, and Nebius Group (NBIS), down about 12%, helped wipe out about $260 billion in software market value amid AI trade fatigue.
- Chipmakers Micron Technology (MU) and AMD (AMD) weighed on the Nasdaq 100 ($NDX) as AI- and semiconductor-related stocks led the decline.
- Netflix (NFLX) slipped roughly 2–3% after naming Peter Rice as its new Chief Content Officer to replace Bela Bajaria.
- Tesla (TSLA) fell about 2% after giving back earlier gains on its Roadster unveiling, which highlighted compressed-air thrusters and aerial maneuvers, even as a U.S. appeals court vacated class certification in a California Full Self-Driving lawsuit.
- Energy outperformed as Brent crude (@QA) rose to around $110 per barrel, lifting Matador Resources (MTDR) by about 7% and Antero Resources (AR) by about 6% and supporting a broader rotation into materials and energy over lagging technology and communication services.
- Financials were mixed after earnings, with Travelers (TRV) beating expectations with non-GAAP EPS of $9.18, Citizens Financial (CFG) topping with $1.41 versus $1.38 expected, and Truist (TFC) posting adjusted EPS of $1.16 while reported EPS of $0.56 included restructuring-related charges.
- Initial after-hours reactions to bank earnings, including Citizens Financial (CFG) and Truist (TFC), were muted, with few individual stock moves exceeding 2%.
- U.S. industrial production rose 0.7% in September after a 9:15 AM ET release, while a U.S. budget deficit nearing $2 trillion added to longer-term caution as investors looked ahead to additional earnings.
